notes: The word being lit is the one being sung again. When a sheet was timed a second time — by the AI pass, by the timing nudge, or by the film’s own clock — its word-by-word timing was left behind, every line fell back to sharing its words out evenly, and that is a line that is right with the wrong word inside it. That timing is now recognised by the words of the line, not only by the timestamp in front of it, so it stays with the line it was measured on.

A sheet that was timed again is measured again: the old timing is only reused while the stamps on the screen are the ones it was measured against, instead of for as long as the sheet happens to have the same number of characters.
The word timing is cleared under both of the names the app keeps it by, so a song opened from a search can never keep the word timing of the timing it had before.

The music video’s sound no longer speeds up and slows down. The voice under a sharp picture was being bent by up to eight percent to keep it on the frame, which is a song audibly changing pitch; it is two percent at most now, and only when it is a tenth of a second out.

The film no longer stops for a buffer dip. The picture could be waiting for bytes and the sound was switched off with it, then jumped back on when the frame returned — a film stopping and starting. The sound now carries on, and is only held once the picture has fallen more than a second behind it.

The sound a sharp picture plays is the lightest copy of the film the answer has, not the first one listed: every copy of one upload carries the same sound, and a heavy one was taking the connection the picture needed.
